concerns.text: The plan proposes 'streaming' data to fit memory but simultaneously requires 'B-spline basis expansion' with 'adaptive selection (GCV/AIC)' for the *entire* ensemble. GCV/AIC optimization typically requires access to the full covariance structure or at least the full set of time-series to determine the optimal basis dimension $K$ globally. Streaming data prevents the calculation of global fit statistics required for adaptive selection, forcing a choice between invalid local selection or memory overflow. The plan does not resolve this methodological conflict.

The stability metric is defined as 'Correlation of eigenfunction loadings between the subsample and the full ensemble.' In fPCA, eigenfunctions (modes) are not unique up to sign and can rotate within the subspace of equal eigenvalues. A simple correlation of loadings is methodologically insufficient to assess stability; it fails to account for subspace rotation (Procrustean rotation) or sign flipping. Without a Procrustean alignment step, the 'stability' metric may report high variance due to arbitrary rotation rather than true instability, invalidating the robustness claim (Constitution Principle VI).

The plan states 'Linear interpolation will be applied to gaps before basis expansion.' For climate time-series with seasonal cycles and high-frequency variability, linear interpolation introduces artificial linearity and distorts the derivative structure required for fPCA. This preprocessing step risks biasing the extracted eigenfunctions, particularly for modes representing high-frequency variability (e.g., ENSO), violating the 'Spatiotemporal Structure Fidelity' principle (Constitution Principle VII). A spline-based imputation or state-space model would be methodologically superior.
